models._description: Adds max_time_between_keys_in_ms to session_info for the scan buffer

behavioral_notes.observation: The classification engine of the framework, invisible to metadata. parse_barcode routes 'urn:' codes to parse_uri (GS1 EPC URI) and everything else to parse_nomenclature_barcode, which iterates self.rule_ids in `sequence asc` order and, for the first rule whose encoding and pattern both match, returns a dict {type, code, value, base_code, encoding}. Per rule it first applies upc_ean_conv (prefix a '0' to convert UPC-A->EAN-13 or strip a leading '0' for EAN-13->UPC-A) so a code can be tried under the other encoding, then calls check_barcode_encoding (length + check-digit validation). type 'alias' rewrites the scanned code to rule.alias and keeps scanning; any other type (product, and the lot/weight/price/package types extended by downstream modules) is returned. This ordered-regex + check-digit dispatch is what turns one raw scanned string into a typed business reference, and it is pure method logic no field/relation can express.

Decodes embedded numeric content (quantity / weight / price) from the barcode. The pattern grammar uses a single `{N..D..}` brace group where N digits are the whole part and D digits the decimal part; match_pattern escapes regex metacharacters, locates the brace group, slices the corresponding barcode substring into whole_part + '0.'+decimal_part to compute match['value'] as int+float, then rebuilds 'base_code' with the variable digits zeroed out (the stable code printed on the product master). So scanning a weight-embedded EAN like 21xxxxx<weight>C yields both the product base_code and the decoded weight value in one pass — embedded-quantity/price decoding that exists only in this method.

GS1 EPC-URI / RFID parsing. For 'urn:...' tags it splits the identifier (lgtin, sgtin, sgtin-96/198, sscc, sscc-96) and the data segment, reassembles the GS1 company prefix + item reference + indicator into a GTIN product barcode (appending get_barcode_check_digit), and returns a LIST of typed results: GTIN tags emit a {type:'product'} plus {type:'lot'} (tracking number) pair, while SSCC tags emit a {type:'package'}. The -96/-198 variants strip the leading filter element of data. This is how an RFID/GS1 URI scan is decomposed into product + lot/serial + package references; none of it is reverse-engineerable from the 3 ORM models.

A @api.constrains('pattern') ValidationError guard, not visible as a plain field. It enforces the `{N*D*}` brace grammar at write time: rejects more than one brace pair, empty braces, braces not of the form N-then-D, the literal '*' (suggesting '.*'), and any pattern that does not compile as a regex once the brace group is stripped. Combined with _order = 'sequence asc, id', this is the integrity layer that keeps the ordered rule set well-formed so parse_nomenclature_barcode's first-match-wins iteration is deterministic.

The server side of the scan-anywhere contract. barcodes.barcode_events_mixin is an AbstractModel exposing a non-stored _barcode_scanned Char; its @api.onchange('_barcode_scanned') fires like an onchange when the form widget writes a scanned code, clears the field, and delegates to on_barcode_scanned(barcode) (NotImplementedError by default — concrete models such as stock pickings override it). ir.http.session_info is overridden to inject barcode.max_time_between_keys_in_ms (default 150 ms, from ir.config_parameter) into the web session, which is exactly the inter-keystroke threshold the JS keystroke buffer reads. These two hooks bind the Python ORM to the OWL scan layer.

behavioral_notes.element: frontend (OWL/JS scan-capture + parser + widgets — gap #3, static/src)
behavioral_notes.observation: The substance of this module is JS, not Python (7 JS / 3 XML). barcodeService (static/src/barcode_service.js, registry services:'barcode') installs a document.body 'keydown' listener implementing the keystroke-buffer heuristic: it accumulates printable keys into bufferedBarcode, ignores special keys, treats Enter/Tab as terminators, and flushes via a setTimeout of maxTimeBetweenKeysInMs (session.max_time_between_keys_in_ms || 150) — distinguishing a fast hardware scanner burst from human typing, with a hidden off-screen input + mobileChromeHandler fallback for mobile Chrome. It emits a 'barcode_scanned' EventBus event. barcodeGenericHandlers (barcode_handlers.js, services:'barcode_handlers') listens and dispatches OBT* (barcode_trigger element clicks) and OCD* navigation commands (OCDEDIT/OCDSAVE/OCDNEXT...) via Macro. BarcodeHandlerField (fields:'barcode_handler') and FloatScannableField (fields:'field_float_scannable') wire scans into form fields; barcode_parser.js (BarcodeParser) is the line-for-line JS port of the Python nomenclature/check-digit/GS1-URI algorithm so the same classification runs client-side; BarcodeScanner / ManualBarcodeScanner (static/src/components) provide the camera (BarcodeDetector / ZXing) and manual-entry dialogs, with audio/error.{mp3,ogg} feedback. None of this is in Python metadata.

it_architecture.application: barcodes (Barcode nomenclature/parsing framework + scan-anywhere OWL capture layer)
logical_data_erm: res.company -> barcode.nomenclature (nomenclature_id, active nomenclature per company)
information_flows: no HTTP routes: the module ships no controllers; it is consumed as a model/mixin API + OWL service, not a service surface
scan capture: browser keydown burst -> barcodeService keystroke buffer -> 'barcode_scanned' EventBus event -> BarcodeHandlerField/FloatScannableField/barcodeGenericHandlers
server hook: barcode_handler widget writes _barcode_scanned -> barcodes.barcode_events_mixin.on_barcode_scanned (overridden by stock/pos/mrp) acts like an onchange
classification: parse_barcode -> ordered barcode.rule regex + check-digit -> typed result {product/lot/weight/price/package} (mirrored client-side by BarcodeParser)
config: ir.http.session_info injects barcode.max_time_between_keys_in_ms into the web session for the JS buffer; res.company.nomenclature_id selects the active rule set

capabilities: Capture a Scanned Code Anywhere in the UI (hardware-scanner keystroke buffer + camera + manual entry)
Define & Maintain Barcode Nomenclatures and ordered Rules (reference data)
Parse & Classify a Barcode into a typed business reference (product / lot / weight / price / package)
Decode embedded quantity / weight / price from a barcode pattern
Parse GS1 / EPC-URI and RFID tags (GTIN, SSCC) into product + lot/serial + package
Validate encoding via EAN/UPC check digits and UPC<->EAN conversion
Provide the on_barcode_scanned mixin + scannable field widgets other apps extend
value_streams: Scan-to-Action: physical scan -> keystroke buffer -> parse/classify -> on_barcode_scanned handler in the consuming app (stock/pos/mrp) acts on the record
Configure-Nomenclature: admin defines barcode.nomenclature + ordered barcode.rule set -> assigned to res.company -> governs every downstream parse
information_concepts: parsed-barcode result {type, code, value, base_code, encoding}
policies: barcode.rule._check_pattern (@api.constrains): enforces the {N*D*} brace grammar / single brace pair / valid-regex pattern integrity
barcode.nomenclature._unlink_except_default (@api.ondelete): blocks deletion of the default nomenclature
barcode.max_time_between_keys_in_ms (ir.config_parameter, default 150 ms): scanner-vs-typing discrimination threshold
rule ordering policy: _order='sequence asc, id' makes parsing first-match-wins and deterministic
stakeholders: Warehouse / shop-floor / POS operator (scans codes during operations)
ERP / inventory administrator (maintains nomenclatures and rules)
Module developer (stock, pos, mrp, point_of_sale, stock_barcode — overrides on_barcode_scanned and reuses the parser/service)

classification.rationale: barcodes is a cross-cutting scanning/identification framework — firm technical infrastructure (Porter support activity; Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support'), not a value-creating primary activity of any one value chain/shop/network. It owns no business object of its own beyond barcode.nomenclature/barcode.rule reference data and the barcodes.barcode_events_mixin; it has 0 HTTP routes and ~655 py LOC, and its real substance is the OWL/JS scan-capture buffer, parser and widgets in static/src (gap #3) that EVERY scanning app (stock, stock_barcode, point_of_sale, mrp) reuses. It is a shared technical capability that underpins 4.0 'Deliver Physical Products / Logistics' (warehouse/POS scanning) but is itself the identification-and-input platform, not the logistics process — so it classifies as APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' (develop & manage the application capability / IT service that delivers barcode identification across the suite), mirroring the precedent set for the 'web' framework module. 4.0 was considered because barcodes is consumed almost entirely by inventory/logistics flows, but rejected: those flows live in stock/pos and merely call into this infrastructure; nothing here advances a logistics value stream by itself. 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities' was also considered (it is a reusable capability others build on) but rejected because barcodes is a concrete running runtime/library, i.e. IT delivery (8.0), not governance/portfolio management.

standard_capabilities: Configurable barcode nomenclatures with ordered, regex-pattern rules (Default Nomenclature + GS1 nomenclature shipped as data)
Server- and client-side parsing of a scanned code into a typed reference (product / lot / weight / price / package / alias)
Embedded quantity / weight / price decoding via the {N*D*} pattern grammar
EAN-8 / EAN-13 / UPC-A check-digit validation and automatic UPC<->EAN conversion
GS1 / EPC-URI and RFID (GTIN, SSCC) tag parsing
Scan-anywhere hardware-scanner capture (inter-keystroke-timing buffer), camera scanner, and manual-entry dialog
barcode_handler / field_float_scannable form widgets and the barcodes.barcode_events_mixin.on_barcode_scanned hook for other apps
OBT* element-trigger and OCD* navigation barcode commands
typical_fits: Out-of-box EAN/UPC product scanning in Inventory, POS and Manufacturing with the default nomenclature
Adding a custom rule (type + encoding + pattern) to recognize a new code family without code
Switching a company to the GS1 nomenclature for GS1-128 / weight-embedded barcodes
Reusing the on_barcode_scanned mixin to make a new model react to scans
common_gaps: New parsed barcode TYPES beyond the shipped selection require Python (extend barcode.rule.type + the consuming model's on_barcode_scanned) — gap #3/code
Non-Code128/EAN/UPC symbologies or proprietary encodings need custom rules or parser work
Tuning scanner timing (barcode.max_time_between_keys_in_ms) for unusual hardware
Camera scanning depends on the browser BarcodeDetector / ZXing support and HTTPS context
No external integration surface (gap #7: 0 HTTP call sites, no SDK/API keys) — purely in-suite infrastructure
drive_hints: odoo shell: env['barcode.rule'].search_read([], ['name','sequence','encoding','type','pattern']) to view the ordered rule set
odoo shell: env['ir.http'].session_info()['max_time_between_keys_in_ms'] to confirm the scan-buffer threshold injected into the client
browser: focus any backend form and emit a fast keystroke burst ending in Enter to fire the 'barcode_scanned' EventBus event
